trigger: async/concurrency + cross-process file locking + irreversible filesystem writes

doubts.claim_under_doubt: when commit hits org_chart_lead_exists (409), nothing was written — 'A different lead already exists at this id. Pick a different lead id.'
doubts.disproof_attempt: commitCore performs the three writes in strict order charter.md -> daemon-config.json -> org-chart.json, and ONLY the org-chart.json write (writeOrgChartLead) has a conflict check comparing the existing entry to the submitted one. writeDaemonConfigAddition has NO such check — it unconditionally overwrites leadProjectRoots[leadId]/leadActionIds[leadId]/leadPluginDirs[leadId] with whatever the current request submitted, every time it is called, regardless of what happens afterward. So a commit for a leadId that already exists on disk with DIFFERENT content: (1) writes charter.md (no lock, no conflict check at all — silently clobbers any existing charter.md at that leadId path); (2) writes daemon-config.json's entries for that leadId (locked, but unconditional overwrite, no conflict check); (3) only THEN discovers the collision in writeOrgChartLead and returns 409 org_chart_lead_exists, leaving org-chart.json itself untouched. Net result: org-chart.json still shows the pre-existing (real) lead's config, but daemon-config.json's leadProjectRoots/leadActionIds/leadPluginDirs for that leadId now point at the REJECTED proposal's project path / action id / plugin dirs, and charter.md may now contain the rejected proposal's prose. This is a silent, on-disk mismatch between org-chart.json (source of truth for 'which leads exist and their settings') and daemon-config.json (source of truth for 'where each lead's process runs') for an ALREADY-ACTIVE, real lead — surfacing only after the next leadwright daemon restart, misdirecting that lead to the wrong project root / action / plugin dirs, with the user told nothing was written. Crucially this needs NO race at all: any ordinary operator who submits a leadId that already exists (typo, forgotten prior setup, no client-side uniqueness check exists anywhere in the wizard — grepped NameIdDomainStep.tsx and the rest of client/src/components/wizard/LeadSetupWizard, no leadId-uniqueness check before commit) triggers it deterministically, every time. It's also invisible to the digest-staleness guard: mergeLeadProposal (leadwright-proposal-merge.ts) unconditionally overwrites orgChart.leads[leadId] with the submitted lead before hashing, so the 'fresh re-check' digest computed in commitCore is identical whether or not that leadId already exists on disk — verdict_stale can never catch a same-id collision, so the org-chart write's late conflict check is the ONLY defense, and it is not applied to the two writes that already ran ahead of it.
doubts.file: server/src/external/org/commit.ts (write ordering, lines 141-192), server/src/external/org/commit-writes.ts (writeDaemonConfigAddition has no conflict check vs. writeOrgChartLead's, lines 69-124), server/src/external/org/leadwright-proposal-merge.ts (mergeLeadProposal always overwrites the target leadId, lines 75-76)
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Either (a) add an upfront existence/conflict check against the freshly-read org-chart.json's leads[leadId] BEFORE any write runs (charter/daemon-config/org-chart), returning 409 org_chart_lead_exists immediately with zero side effects — the check materials (fresh org-chart read) are already in hand at that point in commitCore; and/or (b) give writeDaemonConfigAddition the same idempotency/conflict semantics writeOrgChartLead already has (refuse to overwrite an existing differing entry for leadId rather than silently clobbering it), as defense in depth. Note commit.test.ts's own 'leaving the org chart untouched' test (server/src/external/org/commit.test.ts, ~line 168) only asserts org-chart.json's post-conflict state and never asserts daemon-config.json's — adding that assertion would fail today and demonstrate the bug directly.

summary: 1 high doubt (concurrency/ordering + reversibility + blast radius): a duplicate-leadId commit — reproducible with zero concurrency, just an operator resubmitting an existing id — passes the digest-staleness guard (which cannot see same-id collisions because mergeLeadProposal always overwrites the target key before hashing), then silently corrupts daemon-config.json's entries for an ALREADY-ACTIVE lead before the late org-chart.json conflict check finally rejects the request with a message implying nothing was written. Symlink-escape TOCTOU (check-then-write-by-path in org-file-lock.ts / commit-writes.ts) was attacked and found to be an intentional, already-reviewed risk posture identical to decisions-lock.ts's documented precedent (re-check before AND immediately after lock acquisition, accepted to not extend into arbitrary work inside the critical section) — not re-flagged per the accepted-risk instructions. The leadwright-preflight-transport.ts subprocess call (timeout, output-byte cap, JSON-shape validation, fail-closed on unparsable/empty stdout, error/EPIPE handling) held up under adversarial reading — no gap found. VerdictStep.tsx's auto-retry-once-on-409 effect was traced for stale-closure/loop risk and found sound: the autoRetried flag guards re-entry correctly, refetch always uses the current render's proposal/queryFn, and commit is never auto-resubmitted (only auto re-verdicted) — a genuine 'no bug found' after an honest attempt, not a skim.
resolution: FIXED (this session, same run). commit.ts now reads the freshly-fetched org-chart.json's leads[leadId] and — via the SAME canonicalStringify comparison writeOrgChartLead already used — short-circuits to 409 org_chart_lead_exists BEFORE writeCharterFn, writeDaemonConfigAddition, or writeOrgChartLead is ever called, whenever a DIFFERENT lead already occupies leadId. An identical-content resubmission (the idempotent-retry case) still proceeds through all three writes unchanged. commit.test.ts's existing 'leaving the org chart untouched' test was extended to also assert daemon-config.json is untouched and writeCharterFn was never invoked — this assertion would have failed before the fix and passes after it. Verified: tsc --noEmit clean, full server suite 4021/4021 passed.
